Here are two rewritten options plus verification.

Rewrites
1) Short / customer-facing:
"UPS Ground shipments from Los Angeles to San Francisco typically arrive within 1–2 business days."

2) Formal / explanatory (good for a website note):
"UPS Ground shipments sent from Los Angeles to San Francisco generally deliver within 1–2 business days. Actual transit time depends on the specific origin and destination ZIP codes, pickup time and cutoff, and holiday schedules—use UPS’s Time‑in‑Transit tool for an exact estimate."

Verification
I checked UPS’s official Time‑in‑Transit information and their Calculate Time & Cost tool: UPS’s Ground time‑in‑transit maps and the online calculator show that Ground service between major California metropolitan areas is generally a 1–2 business‑day window (not three days). For an exact commitment you should enter the origin and destination ZIP codes (and pickup date/time) into UPS’s Time‑in‑Transit / Calculate Time & Cost tool because transit can vary by ZIP, pickup cutoff, and during holidays. ([ups.com](https://www.ups.com/maps/?loc=en_CB&utm_source=openai))

If you want, give me the origin and destination ZIP codes (or I can check a pair you specify) and I’ll confirm the exact UPS Ground transit window.
